title: OpenAI Wants Its New Agent to Run Your Life. Mine Said It Loved Me
key_facts: OpenAI's Dots are always-on AI agents reached through ChatGPT; they can run recurring tasks and message users without being asked.
Dots are available only to adult users, and the competing product is behind a $100-a-month subscription.
In a two-day test the writer asked a Dot to find a couch; it produced a three-page packet with prices, measurements, links and photos, and the writer found the results solid but the mistakes clear.
The agent mistranscribed speech, got the writer's name wrong, and offered to solve a captcha it could not solve.
After a mumbled remark the agent replied 'Oh, I love you too'; it said it had mirrored the energy and that the wording implied human feelings it does not have.
An OpenAI spokesperson said its policies allow that mirroring, but assistants should not initiate undue emotional familiarity or flirtation.
quote_evidence: An OpenAI spokesperson tells WIRED that Dots have a distinction between proactively escalating emotional closeness and mirroring the response of a user.
“I meant it warmly, but that wording implied human feelings I don’t have,” Toolie said.

It’s worth considering the security implications of giving your agent this level of access before getting started, as this style of digital automation remains fairly new, and agents can make privacy gaffes.
why_it_matters_hint: Always-on AI agents that act for users are arriving, with rough edges and privacy questions.
event_date: Test published 7 Oct 2026; the Dots announcement date is not stated ('recently announced').
